high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Venetian colored-glass illustration inside a Murano bead workshop: an artisan compares one unfamiliar murrine slice with three fixed pattern cradles, places it in the plain fallback dish when none matches, and leaves the carousel unchanged, showing that classification selects declared outcomes but cannot invent a destination.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A compact Murano glass workshop has soot-dark brick walls, an arched furnace opening at upper left and a matte stone floor. Furnace light forms flat amber shapes rather than photographic illumination. Translucent cobalt, ruby, emerald, amber and milk-white glass colors construct the entire illustration, with no written shop sign, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, flowchart, book, tablet, textile panel, screen, national flag or heraldic crest.

elements.desc: Freestanding brick-and-iron glass furnace at upper left, with one open working mouth containing an even amber interior and one closed annealing chamber below. A plain iron rest projects before the opening for the glass cane. The furnace carries no maker name, temperature number, gauge, arrow, instruction plaque, sacred image, royal device, digital control or photographic reflection.

Adult Murano glass artisan seated beside the furnace, light olive skin, dark wavy hair tied under a cream headscarf, cobalt work shirt, rust-red apron and dark trousers. With a focused expression, the artisan holds one cooled irregular murrine slice in brass tweezers above the fallback dish; the other hand remains away from the fixed cradles and no authoritative badge appears.

Low circular iron sorting carousel occupying the center, built with exactly three colored glass cradles and one plain shallow fallback dish. The fixed cradles contain a ruby six-petal flower, an emerald spiral and a cobalt star pattern. The carousel has no empty socket for another category, movable extension, writing, number, arrow, screen, hierarchy marker or decorative border.

Unfamiliar cooled murrine slice held directly above the plain fallback dish, its asymmetrical amber center surrounded by five unequal milk-white lobes that match none of the three fixed cradle patterns. The slice remains a small solid piece of glass with chipped edges, not a symbol, letter, numeral, badge, coin, shield, label, magical seal or glowing command token.

Long multicolored murrine cane resting horizontally on a dark iron rack at lower right, assembled from bundled ruby, cobalt, emerald and milk-white rods around a plain core. Several freshly cut slices remain aligned beside its end, showing repeated material from one source without creating new sorting destinations. No brand, signature, written recipe, measuring chart, arrow, book or electronic tool appears.
